newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wheat industry fears new trade war.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wheat industry fears new trade war.

text.p: The Australian wheat industry would not survive a new trade war with Argentina, the European Union and other major world grains producers at current prices, Jeff Arney, president of the Grains Council of Australia (GCA), said.
Arney was reacting to the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) A$15.00 a tonne cut in its estimated pool price for all wheat grades apart from durum.
The cut brought the estimated pool price for benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW) to A$175.00 a tonne from A$245.00 a tonne in May, a 29 percent fall.

This was a direct result of volatility in the international grain market as a consequence of improved seasonal conditions in the major producing countries of the U.S. and the European Union (EU), coupled with Argentina aggressively flooding the market to quit increased production, Arney said in a statement.
GCA was concerned that the U.S., EU and Argentina had significant tonnage for export even allowing for some stock re-building, he said.
The Australian wheat industry would compete fairly with major competitors on quality and price, he said.

GCA would press its concerns on the Australian Minister for Primary Industries John Anderson at an industry roundtable on November 8 before Anderson left for the World Food Summit in Rome on November 13-17, he said.
The summit would enable Anderson to have direct access to EU Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler and External Relations Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan after the summit, he said.
"But at these new price levels we will not survive a new trade war," he said.

The EU had recently doubled export subsidies to about A$20 a tonne equivalent and there were real fears that these may increase again to about A$30 a tonne with the EU recently making a sale at the higher level, he said.
"This escalation by the EU is disturbing and has the potential to extract a similar response from the U.S. by the re-introduction ... of its export enhancement programme," he said.
